bee: noun. A flying insect, of the clade Anthophila within the hymenopteran superfamily Apoidea, known for its organised societies (though only a minority have them), for collecting pollen and (in some species) producing wax and honey.
beer: noun. An alcoholic drink fermented from starch material, commonly barley malt; often with hops or some other substance (like gruit) to impart a bitter flavor.
beet: noun. Beta vulgaris, a plant with a swollen root which is eaten or used to make sugar.
bene: noun. A prayer, especially to God; a petition; a boon.
bent: verb. simple past and past participle of bend
beret: noun. A type of round, brimless cap with a soft top and a headband to secure it to the head; usually culturally associated with France.
berth: noun. Chiefly in wide berth: a sufficient space in the water for a ship or other vessel to lie at anchor or manoeuvre without getting in the way of other vessels, or colliding into rocks or the shore.
bet: noun. A wager, an agreement between two parties that a stake (usually money) will be paid by the loser to the winner (the winner being the one who correctly forecast the outcome of an event).
beth: noun. The second letter of the Phoenician alphabet, 𐤁
brr: interjection. Used to express being cold, to show shivering.
enter: verb. To go or come into an enclosed or partially enclosed space.
erne: noun. A sea eagle (Haliaeetus), especially the white-tailed eagle (Haliaeetus albicilla)
eth: noun. A letter (capital Ð, small ð) introduced into Old English to represent its dental fricative, then not distinguished from the letter thorn, no longer used in English but still in modern use in Icelandic, the IPA and other phonetic alphabets to represent the voiced dental fricative "th" sound as in the English word th en.
ether: noun. The substance formerly supposed to fill the upper regions of the atmosphere above the clouds, in particular as a medium breathed by deities.
hen: noun. A female chicken (Gallus gallus), especially a sexually mature one kept for her eggs.
hent: verb. To take hold of, to grasp.
her: determiner. Belonging to her (belonging to that female person or animal, or in poetic or old-fashioned language that ship, city, season, etc).
herb: noun. A plant whose stem is not woody and does not persist beyond each growing season.
here: adverb. In, on, or at this place (a place perceived to be close to the speaker); compare there.
nee: interjection. no, used to express no as a quantity, i.e. not any, like German kein /Dutch geen /French rien.
net: noun. A mesh of string, cord or rope.
nth: adjective. Occurring at position n in a sequence.
reb: noun. Clipping of rebel: a Confederate, especially a Confederate soldier.
ree: noun. Alternative form of rei (“Portuguese real”).
rent: noun. A payment made by a tenant at intervals in order to lease a property.
rente: noun. In France, interest payable by government on indebtedness; the bonds, shares, stocks, etc. that represent government indebtedness.
renter: noun. One who rents property or other goods from another.
ret: verb. To prepare (flax, hemp etc.) for further processing by soaking, which facilitates separation of fibers from the woody parts of the stem.
rete: noun. A network of blood vessels or nerves.
tee: noun. The name of the Latin script letter T / t.
teen: noun. Synonym of teenager: a person between 13 and 19 years old (inclusive).
ten: noun. NATO, ICAO, ITU & IMO radiotelephony code for 10, used only with o'clock to indicate direction.
tern: noun. Any of various seabirds of the subfamily Sterninae (of the family Laridae) that are similar to gulls but are smaller and have a forked tail.
the: article. Used before a noun phrase, including a simple noun The definite grammatical article that shows that the noun phrase that immediately follows it is definitely identifiable......because it has already been mentioned, is to be completely specified in the same sentence, or very shortly thereafter.
thebe: noun. A subdivision of currency, equal to one hundredth of a Botswanan pula.
thee: pronoun. Objective and reflexive case of thou.
there: adverb. In or at a place or location (stated, implied or otherwise indicated) that is perceived to be away from, or at a relative distance from, the speaker (compare here).
three: noun. NATO & ICAO radiotelephony clear code (spelling-alphabet name) for the digit 3.
tree: noun. A perennial woody plant taller and larger than a shrub with a wooden trunk and, at some distance from the ground, having leaves and branches.
beeth: verb. third-person singular simple present indicative of be.
behen: noun. Any of various plants imported into Europe for the pharmaceutical trade in dried form, so of uncertain identity.
benet: verb. To catch in a net; ensnare.
ber: noun. A fruit-bearing tree (Ziziphus mauritiana); Indian jujube.
bere: noun. Barley, especially four-rowed barley or six-rowed barley.
berthe: noun. A sort of trim added to the neckline of a dress.
ert: verb. To incite; urge on; encourage.
heer: noun. A yarn measure of six hundred yards, or 1/24 of a spindle.
herber: noun. A garden in which herbs and vegetables are grown; a herbarium
herbert: noun. A working-class youth, especially male.
neet: noun. Alternative letter-case form of NEET.
nete: noun. In Ancient Greek musical theory, the highest-pitched fixed note in the farther tetrachord on a lyre, always pitched a perfect fourth above the paramese, with two movable notes between them, the trite (lower in pitch) and the paranete (higher in pitch).
rebent: verb. simple past and past participle of rebend
reen: noun. A running waterway that links a ditch or stream to a river.
rerent: verb. To rent (something) again, especially to a new tenant.
rethe: adjective. Fierce; cruel; savage; stern; zealous; ardent; keen.
teer: verb. To stir, as a calico - printer 's sieve.
